captive_summary: Altamira is an onshore import/regas terminal using open-rack (seawater) vaporizers with no on-site gas combustion equipment; its documented purpose is piping regasified gas to the adjacent CFE-area combined-cycle plants (CCC Altamira II, III&IV, and V), the opposite of captive power.
confirmed_how: hydrocarbons-technology.com project page: terminal uses 'open rack vaporisers' and CFE 'agreed to buy 5.2bcmpa of regasified LNG for 15 years from Altamira... used for power generation to support existing and future industry.' The 2004 SEMARNAT environmental impact statement (MIA) for the connecting pipeline states the line's purpose is to supply 'turbinas para la generación eléctrica' at the CCC Altamira V power plant, and describes the Puerto Industrial de Altamira as already hosting CCC Altamira II and CCC Altamira III & IV — i.e. the terminal feeds these external CFE-area plants, it does not self-generate.

captive_summary: Never built. Pemex's proposed $6-billion liquefaction plant at Salina Cruz, Oaxaca was announced at an investor conference in November 2014 (targeted 2020 start), was met with analyst skepticism (no track record, insufficient domestic gas), and Pemex was still seeking strategic partners — it never reached FID (GEM shows no FID year) or a published engineering design.
confirmed_how: University of Texas LACP / Platts (Ronald Buchanan), 10 Nov 2014: Pemex Gas director Alejandro Martinez presented the Salina Cruz liquefaction plan to potential investors in Houston; analysts George Baker and David Shields publicly doubted feasibility ('Pemex lacks a track record'; 'there simply isn't enough gas in Mexico'); the project sought a consortium of 'strategic partners' — i.e. still at the pre-FID investor-courting stage, no equipment/design published.
gogpt_prior_assessment: The two nearby GOGPT-captive plants (Refinería Antonio Dovalí Jaime power station, 115 MW, captive, operating; Cogeneración Salina Cruz power station, 728 MW, captive, announced) are the Pemex Salina Cruz REFINERY's own captive plants — a different industrial host (the refinery, not the never-built LNG export terminal). This is the industrial-host trap: proximity to captive generation at Salina Cruz reflects the refinery complex, not this cancelled LNG project.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Project never built; the captive plants nearby already belong to and are correctly attributed to the Salina Cruz refinery, not this LNG terminal.
status_or_other_findings: None beyond confirming the proposal-only history.
notes: Screen criterion: cancelled-and-never-designed — the project stalled at the investor-pitch stage in 2014 amid analyst skepticism and never secured partners, FID, or a published FEED.

captive_summary: Pichilingue is an onshore (non-floating) New Fortress Energy import/regas terminal purpose-built to pipe gas to three downstream customers — CFE's CTG La Paz and CTG Baja California Sur plants, and NFE's own Amaunet power plant — a documented supply-OUT arrangement, not captive generation at the terminal.

Smith), on NFE's 2020 FID/regas progress: 'The onshore Mexico terminal will supply a power plant at Port of Pichilingue, Baja California Sur' (explicit supply-out framing).
